newsitem.title: USA: Admiral, Army counsel probed for harassment - report.
newsitem.headline: Admiral, Army counsel probed for harassment - report.

text.p: A Navy two-star admiral and the Army's top civilian lawyer are under investigation for sexual harassment, the Washington Post reported Saturday.

The Navy has relieved Rear Adm. R. M. Mitchell Jr., a married man with multiple advanced education degrees, from his duties in Mechanicsburg, Pa. as commander of the Navy's supply system and its more than 10,000 employees, the newspaper said.
Mitchell is alleged to have made repeated advances to a subordinate and created a hostile working environment, according to the report, which added that the investigation was still open.

The Post also said the Defence Department's inspector general was investigating allegations against the Army's general counsel William Coleman III, a longtime friend and Yale Law School classmate of President Clinton.

Quoting sources close to the case, the newspaper said the inspector general had conducted more than 20 interviews based on an anonymous allegation made to a telephone hot line the Army set up in the wake of the sex scandal at its training base in Aberdeen, Md.

The allegations were that Coleman, who is the Army's top legal authority, told offensive sexual jokes in public, listened to rap music with offensive lyrics and on one occasion touched a subordinate in an offensive manner at an office luncheon, the Post said.
"My client is cooperating fully and we absolutely deny any allegation of sexual harassment," Coleman's attorney Arthur Culvahouse told the newspaper.
